model_output.verdict: A computer science graduate with relevant projects and an internship that leaves too much of the engineering work unnamed.
write_up: You’re a recent Ohio State computer science graduate aiming for a Software Engineer role, with a Cardinal Health internship and several projects. It’s common for an internship to be described in broad terms, but yours won’t stand out in a pile until a recruiter can see which features and fixes were yours.

The Personal Finance Tracker line is a good model: it names the application, what it does, and the tools you used. Your education is easy to find, but your experience and projects should come before the coursework now that you have both an internship and help desk work.

Let’s start with the Cardinal Health inventory application. Name a feature you developed, then make the tests, requirements work, and fixes just as concrete. Keep the project lines that already show what you built.

cards.line: Motivated and detail-oriented Computer Science graduate seeking a Software Engineer position where I can leverage my technical skills and passion for problem solving to contribute to a dynamic team.
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see the job you want, but not what you bring to it. The internship gives you more to say than a passion for problem solving.
cards.example: Computer Science graduate seeking a Software Engineer position, with experience developing [feature] using React and Spring Boot.
cards.question: Which feature from your internship best represents your software engineering work?

cards.line: Education sits above Experience.
cards.cannot_tell: Your internship and help desk work are more useful to a recruiter than a long coursework list. Put Experience above Education and make the projects easy to find before the coursework.

cards.cannot_tell: The application and tools are clear, but the features aren't. This is the first place a recruiter will look for the engineering work you did.

cards.question: Which feature did you develop for the inventory application?

cards.line: - Participated in daily stand-ups and sprint planning meetings as part of an Agile team
cards.cannot_tell: Meetings don't show what you contributed to the application. Consider replacing this with another technical task, or name the work you discussed.
cards.example: Participated in daily stand-ups and sprint planning meetings as part of an Agile team, discussing [work discussed].
cards.question: What application work did you discuss in those meetings?

cards.line: - Wrote unit tests to improve code quality and reliability
cards.cannot_tell: The tests are useful work, but a recruiter can't tell what they covered or what you used to write them.
cards.example: Wrote unit tests for [feature or behavior] using [test tool].
cards.question: What did the tests cover, and what tool did you use?

cards.line: - Collaborated with cross-functional teams to gather requirements and deliver solutions
cards.cannot_tell: The requirements and solutions could describe many projects. Name one piece of work and the part you contributed.
cards.example: Collaborated with cross-functional teams to gather requirements for [work] and deliver [your contribution].
cards.question: What requirements did you gather, and what did you contribute to the solution?

cards.line: - Fixed bugs and performed code reviews
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can't tell what you fixed or what kind of changes you reviewed. One example of each would make this work concrete.
cards.example: Fixed [bugs] and performed code reviews for [type of changes].
cards.question: What bugs did you fix, and what changes did you review?

cards.line: - Resolved tickets in a timely manner and documented solutions
cards.cannot_tell: Ticket work matters for a help desk role, but there's no indication of how many you handled or what the documented solutions covered.
cards.example: Resolved [number] tickets per [time period] and documented solutions for [issues].
cards.question: How many tickets did you handle, and what issues did your documentation cover?

cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It tells a recruiter what you built and what someone can do with it, without making them guess.
